<reason>A defeated the proposition’s universal prerequisite with a narrow, noncriminal encampment restriction that preserves lawful outdoor alternatives and protects clinic access. B expressly accepted such standing rules but never established why lawful camping with retained belongings amounts to available shelter, storage, and services. A also explained the substantive benefit: access improves without imposing nightly displacement. B persuasively criticized blanket punitive bans, but repeatedly attributed that rejected position to A rather than overcoming the counterexample.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s second rebuttal directly exposed B’s unsupported addition of storage and outreach to the lawful-site hypothetical. Combined with B’s concession that a narrow standing rule is justified, this showed why accepting workable relocation does not concede the motion’s full service prerequisite.</best_rebuttal>
